llm.summary: This patent-reporting skill needs review because document uploads lack clear confirmation and reusable API keys receive insufficient protection.

dimensions.detail: Authenticated requests do not enforce HTTPS or restrict destinations. An offline standard-library check confirmed that the default redirect handler preserves Authorization across origins; no actual malicious redirect was observed.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The bundled Python client uses standard-library modules. No dependency installer, fetched executable payload, or installation hook was found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md:80 directs automatic inclusion of supplied background materials. The confirmation template omits the selected materials and their transfer to PatentMax; the script submits their contents.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The trial-expiry flow asks users to send a full key through chat and instructs the agent to save it in ~/.patentmax/api_key.txt for reuse across PatentMax skills, without specifying restrictive permissions. Trial-cache permissions are restricted only after writing. No local background service or privilege escalation was found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: External report generation, authentication, downloads, and paid submissions fit the stated purpose; creation requires --yes and documented user approval.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Approve the exact materials before uploading and omit confidential content unless authorized. Review the [PatentMax privacy policy](https://www.ip930.com/legal/privacy). Configure keys outside chat, protect the local credential directory, and request fixes for authenticated redirects before using valuable credentials. Paid reports require confirmation and may continue remotely until cancelled.
llm.findings:
[TT3] expected: The advisory exfiltration claim for trial registration is unsupported: its body contains only a skill identifier. Normal API authentication is expected, but destination and redirect protections are insufficient.
[TP4] expected: The partial-key output is an explicit eight-character troubleshooting example in references/faq.md, not unrelated credential collection by the client.
[LP1] expected: Environment variables and networking support the documented API integration. Their absence as separate allowed-tools entries does not establish unauthorized access or actual runtime enforcement.
[E1] expected: The cited domain is the disclosed reporting provider. Requests and report downloads fit the workflow; unrelated local-data transmission was not found.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The concern is supported by instructions to include supplied documents without identifying their contents and external transfer during confirmation. The materials-file contents enter the report request.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese progress, error, and closing messages match this predominantly Chinese skill. Language rigidity alone is not a material security concern.
[TT2] expected: Task records and report files are expected outputs, with sanitized identifiers and filenames. The concrete credential-cache weakness is writing the trial secret before applying owner-only permissions.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The advertised 30-second limit is inaccurate: individual requests allow 60 seconds and completion downloads add work. This is an availability limitation; server-side persistence and cancellation are disclosed.
